options.title: Is the School Answer for How Planes Fly Wrong?
options.first_line: The school answer for how an A380's wing lifts it is wrong, and NASA says so.
options.first_frame: An Airbus A380 wing already slicing through a dark wind tunnel, glowing streamlines splitting at its front edge.

options.title: Why Does an A380's Wing Actually Lift It?
options.first_line: Why does this wing lift an Airbus A380 off the ground? It isn't the reason you learned.
options.first_frame: A close dolly along the A380's wing as streamlines bend down off its back edge, a small 'A380' label on the wing root.

options.title: Top Air vs Bottom Air: Which Reaches the Back First?
options.first_line: Two puffs of air split at the front of a wing. You were told they meet again at the back. They don't.
options.first_frame: Two glowing air puffs split at a wing's leading edge, the top one already racing ahead over the curve.

why: A famous plane most viewers have flown in, with an open 'why does it lift?' that neither the title nor the first line answers, so you have to stay; A and C already give away that the school answer is wrong or that the air doesn't meet.
